Breaking: Don’t Visit Ko Lipe

📅 23 Feb 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1265 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nomadicmatt

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, after 19 years, I finally went back to Ko Lipe, the Thai island I spent close to a month on in 2006.
  • Sources indicate that there was much to do here but that was the point.
  • It was paradise – and a place a lot of people got stuck.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, after 19 years, I finally went back to Ko Lipe, the Thai island I spent close to a month on in 2006. Back then, it was one of those super off-the-beaten-path destinations that few but the most intrepid travelers visited, where electricity only ran a few hours a day, basic bungalows right on the beach cost something like $2 USD, and there really was a last boat for the season.

Sources indicate that there was much to do here but that was the point. You hung out on the beach, read a book, went snorkeling, went back to the beach, drank beers at the one beach bar on the island, rotated meals between the five restaurants there, and went to bed early.

It was paradise – and a place a lot of people got stuck. Days easily turned into weeks here.

If you asked me what the highlight of all my travels was, I would be the time I spent on Ko Lipe. I made incredible friends, lounged around, got to know the locals, learned a bit of Thai, and, overall, lived that idyllic backpacker life we all dream about.

According to recent reports, over the years, I’ve avoided going back to Ko Lipe because the memory of my time there is so strong that I didn’t want to ruin it. Any re-visit would simply be trying to recreated a magic that couldn’t be recreated because the people that it special wouldn’t be there. I’d be chasing travel ghosts. And, since I know my sleepy paradise has been developed greatly over the years, I was also too afraid seeing that would make me sad.

Tourism in Thailand tends toward the unsustainable. No island really develops in a good way. It’s all build, build, build.

And I didn’t want to see my Ko Lipe like that.

In a recent development, but as I was planning my recent trip through Southeast Asia, returning to Ko Lipe made sense. I was heading down the Indian Ocean side of Thailand on my way into Malaysia and I’d pass by it.

In a recent development, and, since I was looking for a lively place for Latest Year’s Eve, it seemed liked the best choice. I knew there would be travelers there and there were no other nearby islands that would work, especially since Ko Lipe has a boat to Langkawi, which was my next stop.

And I’m sad to report that Ko Lipe took the Ko Phi Phi model of tourism and is now extremely overdeveloped.

Most of the island is now paved over, the old dirt footpaths having become concrete for the cars and construction trucks. Swaths of palm trees are now the sites of high-end resorts with pools (on an island with no natural water supply). Construction of more resorts continues at a fast pace. The coral around the island is dying, a victim of all the boats, anchors, pollution, and overfishing. Beaches are now lined with boats, their exhaust spilling into the ocean, leaving a shiny film you can see as you swim. And the restaurants cater to tourists looking for bad Western food, not great Thai cuisine.

The island’s boom has displaced many locals, who were forced to sell to mainland developers, and much of the island’s workforce is now from the mainland. They see little of the benefits this tourism boom.

So lies Ko Lipe, another victim of Thailand’s all too common overdevelopment and exploitation of limited resources.

In a recent development, I met lots of people there who loved the island. If it’s your first time, I can see why you would love it. After all, the area is postcard perfect, the water is perfectly an azure blue, the sand is a beautiful white, and since you’re surrounded by a national park, a lot of tours take you to some secluded islands.

And, in comparison to Ko Phi Phi, Krabi, or Phuket, it is less developed so I can’t fault someone stepping here for the first time going “wow!”.

But, as I reflect on the island and its overdevelopment, I have come to the same conclusion I have about Ko Phi Phi: people shouldn’t visit.

I’m not against growth, but I’m against this kind of growth. It’s not sustainably managed and going there will only tax the island’s limited resources even further. You can’t put the genie back in the bottle and no local is going to say “sure, I’ll stay broke so you can an idealized vision of the world.”.

And, with so many other islands to visit that are well managed (Ko Lanta, Ko Jum, and Ko Mook, to name three nearby), I think you should skip Ko Lipe.

A visit there will only make things worse.

It has been revealed that it pains me to say that, because it was such a beautiful place, and my original visit had a huge impact on my life. But if we’re going to be good stewards and travelers, sometimes you just have to say enough is enough.

And Ko Lipe is a place where enough is enough.

Go somewhere else that is better managed.

Because your choices do have an impact.

It has been revealed that riding elephants in Thailand went away when consumers became more conscious of it. Eco lodges got significant because of consumers. Overtourism is talked about by consumers as much as it is by locals.

Maybe if enough people start to do something, Ko Lipe will change.

But, at the very least, by not going you are at least no contributing to the problem.

Democrats mulling Iran war funding cutoff strategy

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (615 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tim Kaine, D-Va., talks with reporters in the Capitol on Sept.
  • A group of prominent Senate Democrats is pushing to use a must-pass spending bill to cut off funding for the Iran war, complicating the path toward a bipartisan deal for averting a partial government shutdown next month.
  • Tim Kaine, D-Va., said Thursday he is working on legislative language ending the war that he wants attached to the next continuing resolution that is needed by Dec.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., talks with reporters in the Capitol on Sept. 30. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

A group of prominent Senate Democrats is pushing to use a must-pass spending bill to cut off funding for the Iran war, complicating the path toward a bipartisan deal for averting a partial government shutdown next month.

Recent findings suggest that sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., said Thursday he is working on legislative language ending the war that he wants attached to the next continuing resolution that is needed by Dec. 11, when current funding runs out.

“I know it’s going to be my main push,” he said. “I have to work with colleagues to try to find some language that works. And I’m not there yet, but I’ve told everybody that’s an opportunity.”.

Democratic Sens. Michael Bennet of Colorado, Chris Van Hollen of Maryland, Tammy Duckworth of Illinois and independent Bernie Sanders of Vermont released a statement Thursday that they would oppose any deal that does not include “language that restricts the Trump Administration from using appropriated funds to continue his war against Iran.”.

It has been revealed that “When we vote on appropriations, we intend to fund the government and stop funds for this war,” the senators said. “It is what the American people demand, and what they deserve.”.

It is unlikely that Republicans, who are in control of both chambers of Congress until January, not to mention the Oval Office beyond that, would agree to such a deal.

House Appropriations Chairman Tom Cole, R-Okla., stated earlier this week that “a Republican Congress is not going to send bills to a Republican president that he's going to veto.”.

While ending the war is a top priority of Democrats as they take back power in the new Congress, insisting on doing so this year could lead to a Christmas-time partial government shutdown. If a shutdown starts after Dec. 11, it’s possible it would still be ongoing when Democrats take control of both chambers in January.

But some Democrats appeared to still be weighing how rapidly to push for a cutoff of war funding.

Senate Appropriations ranking member Patty Murray, D-Wash, stated that whether or not Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth remains in his job, “we’re still going to have language stopping this war.”.

She was coy on whether that fight would take place on the anticipated continuing resolution in December or wait until next year when Democrats take back power, saying that lawmakers are “looking at all options.”.

It has been revealed that democrats are committed to ending the "reckless and costly war of choice in Iran," House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., said Thursday. He deferred to House Appropriations ranking member Rosa DeLauro, D-Conn., "to see what’s possible in advance of Dec. 11" in talks with the other top appropriators.

In a recent development, "I don’t want to get out ahead of Congresswoman DeLauro, but House Democrats have uniformly opposed providing any additional money to Donald Trump’s war machine. to Pete Hegseth’s war machine, over in the Middle East," Jeffries mentioned.

It’s not clear how long a potential continuing resolution would last, and DeLauro mentioned earlier this week that she wants it to be as short as possible.

The Office of Management and Budget has not yet submitted “anomalies” — changes to the current spending levels to be included in the continuing resolution — to Congress.

According to recent reports, the administration is considering options including a stopgap bill that would run through March, sources familiar with the talks said. But no decision on the timing covered by the anomalies has been made.

Aris Folley, Jacob Fulton and Michael Macagnone contributed to this report.

Latest Update: 12 Airline Booking Traps That Could Cost You Money in 2026

📅 19 Jun 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2602 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theplanetd

⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Airline websites are not necessarily badly designed, even though they often feel that way.
  • According to recent reports, you start with a flight that looks like it costs $400.
  • After more than 18 years of travel to over 130 countries, we still catch ourselves slowing down to double-check airline bookings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Airline websites are not necessarily badly designed, even though they often feel that way. In many cases, the booking process is doing exactly what it was designed to do: get you focused on the lowest advertised fare before revealing the cost of everything else.

According to recent reports, you start with a flight that looks like it costs $400. By the time you add a carry-on bag, choose a seat, and work through the final checkout screens, the total is suddenly $650.

After more than 18 years of travel to over 130 countries, we still catch ourselves slowing down to double-check airline bookings. The difference now is that we know where the expensive mistakes are usually hiding. We also use flight-search and tracking tools to compare routes and monitor changes. See our guide to the best travel apps for 2026.

The lowest price on the first screen is rarely enough information to tell you which flight is actually cheapest. You need to compare the complete journey, including baggage, seats, fare restrictions, connections, operating airlines, and the risk involved if something goes wrong.

According to recent reports, to avoid costly airline booking mistakes, compare the total price of the journey rather than the advertised base fare. Check the conditions of the exact fare, baggage allowances, operating airline, cabin on every segment, connection times, and whether the flights are issued on one protected ticket.Before paying, compare the flight as a round trip, two one-way tickets, and a multi-city itinerary. Before leaving home, verify your passport, visas or travel authorizations, transit requirements, check-in deadline, and gate-closing time.

These airline booking traps—also common flight-booking mistakes—can turn an apparently cheap ticket into the most expensive option.

One of the first mistakes travellers make is comparing flights by airline logo.

You see the airline you normally use, remember the points sitting in your account, and stop comparing. But loyalty should not convince you to pay hundreds of dollars more for a worse schedule, a more restrictive ticket, or a fare that excludes everything you need.

Recent findings suggest that airline points can still be valuable, especially when you are close to earning useful status or have benefits such as complimentary baggage. But loyalty should be one part of the calculation, not the starting point.

Before choosing an airline, compare:.

Sources indicate that the days of automatically paying more because “this is our airline” are over. Loyalty should follow value, not the other way around.

Basic Economy can be a perfectly reasonable fare. The trap is buying it without understanding what has been removed.

It may work well when you are taking a short flight, travelling with only a small personal item, do not care where you sit, and are confident your looks will not change.

The problem is that airline websites normally display the lowest available fare first. Once you are in booking mode, it is easy to select that number and move forward without reading the restrictions.

You may save $40 on the ticket and then spend $85 adding the carry-on bag you needed from the beginning.

Before booking Basic Economy, price the next fare category. A Standard Economy ticket may cost more initially but include a carry-on bag, checked luggage, seat selection, or greater flexibility.

According to recent reports, also consider whether seat selection genuinely matters. Travellers with children, mobility considerations, medical needs, or a strong need for an aisle or window seat should include that cost when comparing fares.

Do not buy the lowest number. Buy the fare that includes what you actually need.

Airlines do not necessarily sell every Economy Class seat at the same price. Seats are divided into fare classes or pricing tiers, often called fare buckets.

When the cheapest tier sells out, the price can jump even when the aircraft still has many empty seats.

According to recent reports, that is one reason a flight might appear at $480 in the morning and $620 later that day. It does not always mean the plane suddenly filled up. It may mean the least expensive fare class is no longer available.

When you see a noticeable price increase, do not assume you must either pay it immediately or lose the trip.

Start the comparison again and check:.

It has been revealed that A competitor may now be cheaper. In other cases, the next fare level may include baggage, seat selection, or flexibility that makes it better value than the stripped-down ticket you were originally considering. A fare jump is a signal to widen the search, not automatically accept the fresh price.

For the tools we use to compare dates, airports, and fare changes, see our guide to the best travel apps for finding flights.

The standard airline search box encourages travellers to enter a departure city, destination, outbound date, and return date.

That does not mean a traditional round trip is always the cheapest or most efficient way to book.

Before purchasing an expensive international itinerary, compare it three ways:.

An open-jaw ticket means flying into one city and returning home from another.

Industry observers note that for example, if you are travelling through Europe, you might fly into Paris and return from Rome. Even if the airfare is similar to a return ticket from Paris, you could avoid paying for a train or flight back to your starting point. You may also save a hotel night and an entire day of backtracking.

Different airlines can also be used in each direction. One carrier may offer the best outbound flight, while another has a much better return schedule.

It has been revealed that when comparing separate tickets, check baggage fees, fare restrictions, connection risks, and cancellation policies. The goal is not to find the cleverest itinerary. It is to determine which option gives you the best total trip.

With a codeshare flight, the airline selling the ticket may not be the airline flying the plane.

You might purchase the journey through one airline’s website and then arrive at the airport to discover that a partner carrier operates the flight.

Before buying, look for the words “operated by” in the flight details.

Then check the itinerary on both airline websites. Confirm the aircraft, seat map, baggage allowance, terminal, and check-in instructions.

Industry observers note that after booking, make sure you have the operating carrier’s reservation number. The confirmation number issued by the airline selling the ticket may not work on the partner airline’s website.

According to recent reports, codeshares are not automatically bad. They can provide more destinations and useful connections. The problem is that they create a handoff between companies, and that handoff can become confusing when you need assistance.

As we have learned, one of the most expensive sentences in travel can be: “You need to contact the other airline.”.

Mixed-cabin fares are one of the easiest airline traps to miss.

The search result may display a large Premium Economy or Business Class label, making it appear that the entire journey is in the upgraded cabin.

Then you expand the flight details and discover that the 40-minute connection is in Premium Economy while the eight-hour overnight flight is in regular Economy.

We have come close to booking this type of itinerary several times.

Sources indicate that before paying, check the cabin listed beside every individual segment. Make sure the premium seat is on the flight where you will actually benefit from it.

Do not assume one premium segment provides premium benefits throughout the trip.

According to recent reports, screenshot the cabin shown for each flight and confirm that it appears correctly in the final reservation. A mixed-cabin fare is only a deal when the upgraded cabin is on the part of the journey that matters.

There is rarely one simple baggage policy that applies to every passenger flying with an airline.

It has been revealed that do not check only the airline’s general baggage page. Open the conditions attached to the specific fare and route you are considering.

This is especially key when connecting from a transatlantic flight to a smaller airline or low-cost carrier within Europe. A bag accepted on the first flight may be too large, too heavy, or not included on the next one.

In a recent development, A bag fitting inside the overhead compartment does not automatically mean it meets the airline’s rules. Wheels, handles, and outside pockets are normally included when the bag is measured.

Price your luggage before buying the flight. A ticket that appears $30 cheaper can quickly become more expensive once the necessary baggage is added.

Paying for bags online in advance is also frequently less expensive than waiting until the airport, although the difference varies by airline.

According to recent reports, finally, weigh your suitcase at home using a real scale. Picking it up and declaring that it “feels about 20 kilos” is not a reliable baggage strategy.

Once you know your allowance, follow our two-minute checked-bag routine before handing your suitcase over at the airport.

A self-transfer may be the most expensive mistake in this guide.

Recent findings suggest that some search and booking sites combine two separate tickets and display them as one journey. Look for warnings such as:.

The critical detail is that the airlines may not recognize the flights as one protected itinerary.

It has been revealed that if the first flight is delayed and you miss the second one, the second airline may consider you a no-show. You could lose the remaining flights on that reservation and be forced to purchase a upcoming last-minute ticket.

The first airline may not be responsible for helping because it transported you to the destination shown on its ticket.

A self-transfer can also require you to:.

Leaving the international transit area can also trigger entry or transit requirements that would not apply during a normal airside connection.

Self-transfers can work when you have a long buffer, carry-on luggage, an airport you understand, and enough flexibility to absorb a disruption.

We would not use one when connecting to a cruise, wedding, organized tour, or once-daily long-haul flight.

Always compare the self-transfer price with a protected itinerary. The higher fare may not simply be buying convenience. It may be buying the airline’s responsibility to get you to your final destination.

Airlines can sell a connection that technically meets the airport’s minimum requirements.

That does not necessarily mean it is comfortable, sensible, or suitable for you.

A 45-minute connection at a large international airport might involve:.

If a connection makes you nervous while sitting at home, it will not feel better when you are waiting for the aircraft door to open. Choose connection time based on the consequences of missing the next flight.

Sources indicate that A long layover can be inconvenient. A missed connection can cost a full day or derail the entire trip.

It has been revealed that we use third-party flight sites for research. They are useful for comparing airlines, dates, and routing options.

Buying through one is a separate decision.

Sources indicate that A third-party fare may be genuinely cheaper, but make sure you are comparing the same product. It could involve:.

The biggest matter normally appears when the schedule changes or the flight is cancelled.

The airline may tell you to contact the organization that issued the ticket. The booking company may then tell you that only the airline can resolve the flight.

It has been revealed that before buying, find the itinerary through the search site and compare it directly with the airline. When the price difference is small, booking with the airline may be worth it for easier communication during disruptions.

It has been revealed that also check the payment currency. Some booking sites offer to convert the total into your home currency. This feels convenient but may include a less favourable exchange rate.

Sources indicate that when your credit card does not charge a foreign transaction fee, paying in the original currency may be less expensive. Compare the final converted amount and check your card’s fees rather than choosing a currency based on familiarity.

Sources indicate that some of the most expensive travel problems do not happen during booking. They happen at the airport after your hotel, tour, rental car, or cruise has already been paid for.

A valid passport may not be enough to enter your destination or transit through a connecting country.

Depending on your nationality, route, and destination, you may need:.

According to recent reports, A passport can be valid on your departure date and still fail to meet the destination’s entry requirements. Complicated connections are also a good reason to review our international travel safety tips before departure.

It has been revealed that names matter too. The name on your airline ticket should match your passport and any visa or travel authorization. Do not assume that a nickname or commonly used name will be accepted.

Before an international trip, take five minutes to verify:.

Canadian travellers should verify current destination-specific requirements using official government travel advisories and the relevant embassy or immigration authority, since entry and transit rules can change.

Five minutes at home can save the entire trip at the airport. For our complete pre-departure routine, read our travel safety checklist for 2026.

Departure time is when the aircraft is scheduled to leave. It is not the time you should arrive at the gate.

Recent findings suggest that boarding begins earlier, and the gate closes before departure. The exact cutoff depends on the airport, airline, route, and destination.

Once the gate is closed, seeing the aircraft through the terminal window will not save your seat.

According to recent reports, if you miss the flight, the cost may extend far beyond a replacement ticket. You might also lose:.

Build your airport schedule backward from the airline’s check-in, baggage-drop, boarding, and gate-closing deadlines.

According to recent reports, check current security conditions using the airport’s official app or website, but do not treat an estimated wait time as a guarantee. Add time for airport parking, shuttle transportation, baggage drop, security, passport control, terminal changes, and finding the gate.

It is better to have extra time near the gate than to spend the start of your trip running through an airport while your name is being called over the loudspeaker. Arriving early does not help much if your carry-on slows you down at screening. Read our airport security tips and common mistakes before packing.

Before confirming a flight, we recommend checking the entire itinerary one final time.

The best defence against airline booking traps is not a secret search setting or complicated flight hack. It is slowing down long enough to compare the complete journey.

All 12 of these traps work best when travellers are rushing.

In a recent development, we see a low fare, get excited about the trip, and want to finish before the number changes. The booking process then reveals the bags, seats, restrictions, connections, and other costs after we have already become emotionally committed to the flight.

Industry observers note that the cheapest flight is not necessarily the one with the lowest number on the first screen. It is the flight that gets you to your destination without surprise charges, unrealistic connections, or an expensive problem at the airport.

According to recent reports, after more than 18 years of travelling, experience has not made us immune to booking mistakes. It has simply taught us when to stop, reopen the details, and check everything one more time.

Recent findings suggest that take five minutes before pressing confirm. Those five minutes could save hundreds of dollars—or save the entire trip.

Industry News: How the Antigravity 360 Drone Will Change Your Travels

📅 23 Apr 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1540 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nomadicmatt

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • And, while there’s lots of restrictions around them, a lot of travelers take them on road because they produce some amazing sweeping aerial shots.
  • There’s lots of amazing brands out there but one that I think is super cool is the Antigravity A1.
  • I was sent one to use and want to share my experience and why I like this product so much.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Drones are huge. And, while there’s lots of restrictions around them, a lot of travelers take them on road because they produce some amazing sweeping aerial shots.

There’s lots of amazing brands out there but one that I think is super cool is the Antigravity A1. Released in late 2025, attempts to render the traditional gimbal obsolete for a vast segment of creators. By leveraging a dual-lens 360-degree capture system, the A1 records everything in every direction simultaneously. The result is a “fly now, frame later” experience that feels less like piloting a drone and more like directing a virtual camera in a pre-recorded digital environment.

I was sent one to use and want to share my experience and why I like this product so much.

What make’s Antigravity 360’s so special is the two lenses. Most drones feature a single lens that points forward. However, the A1 features two ultra-wide-angle lenses positioned on the top and bottom of the central fuselage that each captures a 200-degree field of view. When those images are combines, they overlap to create a seamless 360-degree sphere.

And, in the final exported footage, the drone itself is digitally removed, creating the illusion of a camera floating in mid-air with no visible means of support.

Recent findings suggest that the sensors themselves are 1/1.28-inch CMOS units. While smaller than the 1-inch sensors found on some “Pro” level photography drones, they are massive compared to typical 360 action cameras. This allows for significantly better low-light performance and a higher dynamic range, capturing details in the highlights and shadows that would typically be lost in the harsh contrast of a midday sun.

Recent findings suggest that most countries require drones weighing 250 grams or more to be registered and subject to stricter flight rules. Antigravity clearly understood the importance of this threshold because they made the A1 to weigh exactly 249 grams with its standard battery meaning it’s not considered a commercial drone so you don’t have to register it.

According to recent reports, and the drone feels remarkably sturdy. It utilizes a high-grade carbon-fiber-reinforced polymer that offers a better strength-to-weight ratio than the standard ABS plastic found in cheaper models. The folding mechanism is satisfyingly tactile, clicking into place with a precision that suggests long-term durability. When folded, the drone is roughly the size of a large smartphone, though about three times as thick.

The Vision Goggles: These are sleek, lightweight, and feature dual 4K micro-OLED displays with a 120Hz refresh rate. The latency is nearly non-existent and they have integrated head tracking. Because the drone is recording in 360 degrees, you aren’t limited to seeing what is in front of the drone. When you turn your head to the left, the goggle feed pans to the left. If you look down, you see the ground passing beneath you. This provides a sense of presence and spatial awareness that is simply impossible with a traditional fixed-camera drone.

Sources indicate that the drone uses a single-handed motion controller. You point the controller where you want to go and pull the trigger to accelerate. Tilt your wrist left to bank, or raise the nose of the controller to climb. It is an incredibly intuitive system that allows even a novice to fly through complex environments within minutes. For professional FPV pilots who prefer the precision of manual acrobatic flight, the A1 does support a traditional “Mode 2” stick controller, but the motion controls are so fluid that most owners will likely never switch back.

Here’s a video of the drone in action:.

The marketing for the Antigravity 360 proudly displays “8K Resolution.” In a traditional camera, 8K means every pixel is packed into a 16:9 rectangle. In 360 video, those pixels are spread across a full sphere. When you “reframe” that 8K sphere into a standard flat video, you are looking at a “crop” of the total image.

The color science is noticeably improved over previous 360 cameras. The A1 features a “Vivid” profile for those who want punchy, social-media-ready colors, and a 10-bit “Log” profile for professional editors who need to match the footage to other cameras in a color-grading suite. The stabilization, powered by Antigravity’s “FlowState” algorithms, is nothing short of miraculous. You can fly in 20mph winds, and the footage remains as steady as if the camera were on a tripod.

It has been revealed that the “Antigravity Studio” app allows you to download footage wirelessly (at speeds up to 80MB/s) and reframe your video using your phone’s gyroscope. You simply watch the video and move your phone around to “film” the scene in real-time. The app also features “Auto-Frame,” an AI tool that identifies subjects and automatically generates a cut that keeps them in focus. For a solo creator, this effectively provides a virtual camera crew that never misses a shot.

According to recent reports, battery technology remains the bottleneck for all small drones. The A1’s standard Intelligent Flight Battery provides a theoretical 24 minutes of flight. In real-world conditions with moderate wind and constant recording, expect closer to 19 or 20 minutes.

While 20 minutes sounds short, the “work per minute” is much higher than a traditional drone. Because you don’t need to re-fly a path to get different angles, a single 20-minute flight can yield the same amount of usable footage as three flights with a Mavic. For those who need more time, the “Pro Battery” (which pushes the weight over 250g) offers a staggering 39 minutes of flight time, though it does compromise the drone’s agility slightly.

In terms of flight dynamics, the A1 is a “cinewhoop” style flyer. It is stable and predictable rather than aggressive and twitchy. It has a top speed of roughly 36 mph, which is plenty for following bikes or cars, but it won’t keep up with a professional racing drone. The “Turtle Mode” is a life-saver; if you crash and end up upside down, the drone can flip itself over using its propellers, allowing you to take off again without a “walk of shame” to recover the aircraft.

The Antigravity 360 is a niche product that is rapidly becoming mainstream.

Sources indicate that the Antigravity 360 (A1) is the most exciting drone I have tested. By removing the need for a gimbal and the stress of manual framing, it allows the pilot to focus on the one thing that truly matters: the story they are trying to tell.

Industry observers note that while the image quality isn’t quite at the level of a high-end cinema drone, and the lenses are admittedly delicate, these are small prices to pay for the creative liberation the A1 provides. It bridges the gap between traditional cinematography and the immersive world of VR.

If you are a creator who is tired of the same old “drone shots” and want to push the boundaries of what is possible in the air, the Antigravity 360 is an essential addition to your toolkit.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Madeira Ports Authority declared that AIDA Cruises celebrated 30 years of partnership with the ports with a gathering on the AIDAprima on November 5 at the Port of Funchal, bringing together institutional partners and representatives of the cruise tourism sector.

The event, part of the cruise line’s “30 Years of Strong Partnership–Destination Dialogue: Shaping the Future Together” program, brought together the Madeira Ports Authority (APRAM, SA), Funchal City Council, AIDA’s shipping agents and shorex agents.

“AIDA Cruises is an crucial partner for the Port of Funchal and Madeira, with a relationship spanning three decades that has contributed to the development and consolidation of cruise tourism in the Region,” noted Paula Cabaco, chairwoman of the board of directors of the Madeira Ports Authority (APRAM, SA).

This relationship, she said, is built on trust, cooperation and joint efforts.

Sources indicate that “For 30 years, AIDA and Madeira have shared a close and trusting partnership. We are sincerely grateful to our partners and the people of Madeira for the openness, hospitality and trust they have shown AIDA and our guests throughout these years,” noted Steffi Heinicke, senior vice president, guest experience and OBR, at AIDA Cruises. “We look forward to continuing this special partnership for many years to come.”.

According to the press release, AIDA Cruises’ ships made 40 calls to Madeira last year, representing more than 23 percent of the total number of passengers at the Port of Funchal.

APRAM added that the partnership has been developed by several entities, including Funchal City Council, and represented at the event by Vice-Mayor Carlos Rodrigues, tourism organizations, authorities and industry stakeholders.

The collaboration also has an environmental dimension, as seen with the tree-planting initiative at Funchal’s Ecological Park.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fincantieri has unveiled more details about the two new ships it will build for Carnival Cruise Line.

Following yesterday’s announcement of a deal for the construction of upcoming vessels between the two companies, Fincantieri has now shared that the ships, scheduled for delivery in 2033 and 2035, will be built at its Marghera shipyard.

Fincantieri noted in a press release that the value of the contract is deemed “very key,” a designation it uses for agreements whose value exceeds €2 billion.

The ships will be 130,000 tons and have around 1,650 guest cabins each, the shipbuilder remarked.

The vessels will be dual-fuel powered, with LNG as their primary fuel.

Additionally, the fresh design has been developed as a multi-brand platform for Carnival Corporation with a view to its potential future implementation across several of its cruise lines.

It has been revealed that “With 12 latest ships now on order for delivery through 2039 across Carnival Cruise Line, Princess and AIDA, we have a strong pipeline that supports our measured approach to growth. The variety of ship sizes and features gives us flexibility to expand the choices and destinations we offer guests,” said Josh Weinstein, CEO of Carnival Corporation.

According to recent reports, “At the same time, each new generation of ships brings advances in technology and efficiency that help us further reduce emissions and our overall environmental footprint. Fincantieri has been a terrific partner throughout this journey, and even after 76 ships and 30 years, there’s still something special about seeing the next one come to life.”.

Industry observers note that pierroberto Folgiero, CEO and managing director of Fincantieri, noted: “Our relationship with Carnival Corporation continues to evolve through a shared ambition to push the boundaries of ship design, technological innovation and sustainability. These vessels embody a new paradigm of shipbuilding, where product innovation goes hand in hand with the transformation of our industrial system.”.

This follows the order for three new Ace-class ships the duo confirmed in July, the first of which, the Carnival Destiny, is already being built at the Monfalcone shipyard.

As previously reported, the first Ace-class vessel will carry the name previously used by the 1996-built Destiny.

Sources indicate that sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., left, has announced a challenge to current Senate Minority Leader Charles Schumer, D-N.Y. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call file photo).

Sen. Chris Van Hollen announced Thursday night that he would run for Senate majority leader, launching a challenge to Sen. Charles E. Schumer of Upcoming York, the current Democratic leader.

Van Hollen, a Maryland Democrat first elected to the Senate in 2016, served in leadership in the House and has been chairman of both the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee. He has said since the midterm elections he was listening to fellow Senate Democrats about the possibility of a run for the top job.

“In this election, the American people called for change. They called for a change from Donald Trump’s disastrous policies but even bigger than that, a change from the status quo that isn’t working for working people,” Van Hollen mentioned in a statement. “It’s now on us to meet this moment, and to do that we need newly introduced leadership. This is not about any one person – it’s about answering the call of the American people. That is why I’m running for Senate Majority Leader.”.

Schumer has already mentioned he has the votes needed to continue serving as the leader.

Recent findings suggest that “I welcome any discussion about the future of our caucus and the important work ahead. I’m proud of what we’ve accomplished together — 55 seats and counting is an amazing result — and I have the votes to continue serving as Democratic Leader. I look forward to leading our new Democratic majority and delivering for the American people,” Schumer remarked in a statement.

Most travellers now fly with several battery-powered items: a phone, laptop, tablet, camera, headphones, smartwatch, portable charger or vape. But packing one of them in the wrong bag can cause real problems at the airport.

In a recent development, in 2026, aviation safety authorities are warning travellers to pay closer attention to lithium batteries after reports that millions of batteries are still being packed incorrectly. The biggest mistake is simple: power banks, portable chargers and spare lithium batteries should not go in checked luggage.

They belong in your carry-on bag or personal item, where they can be reached quickly if they overheat, smoke or catch fire. This matters even more when your carry-on gets taken away at the gate and sent underneath the plane.

No. Power banks, portable chargers and spare lithium batteries should not be packed in checked luggage. They belong in your carry-on bag or personal item, where they can be reached swiftly if they overheat.The same goes for loose camera batteries, spare laptop batteries, rechargeable battery packs, vape devices and phone battery charging cases. If an airline allows a device to be checked, it should be completely powered off, protected from damage and prevented from turning on accidentally.

The safest habit is simple: power banks, spare batteries and removable batteries stay with you. Valuable electronics are usually better in the cabin too.

Power banks are not allowed in checked luggage because they contain lithium batteries that can overheat if damaged, poorly packed, overcharged, exposed to heat or affected by a defect.

Industry observers note that in rare cases, lithium batteries can enter thermal runaway. That means the battery heats faster than it can cool itself down. It may swell, smoke, burn or ignite.

According to recent reports, if that happens in the cabin, passengers and crew can spot the problem quickly. Cabin crews are trained to respond to battery incidents. If the battery is hidden inside a suitcase in the cargo hold, it is much harder to access.

That is why this rule is not just airport red tape. A small charger in the wrong bag can become a serious safety matter.

Before you check a suitcase, look for anything with a loose, spare or removable lithium battery.

Some airlines may allow certain devices with batteries installed in checked luggage if they are completely powered off and protected from damage. But for most travellers, the smarter choice is to keep electronics in the cabin.

Checked bags get dropped, delayed, searched and occasionally sent on their own little vacation. Your laptop does not need that character-building experience.

This is where the rules confuse a lot of travellers.

It has been revealed that A spare battery is any battery that is not installed inside the device it powers. A power bank also counts because it is an external battery used to charge other devices.

A battery installed in a device is different. This includes the battery built into your phone, laptop, tablet, camera, headphones or smartwatch.

Sources indicate that if the battery is loose, removable or used to charge something else, do not check it. The FAA’s lithium battery guidance says power banks and spare lithium batteries must travel in carry-on baggage, not checked luggage.

Gate-checking is one of the easiest ways to accidentally break the battery rule.

Industry observers note that you may pack your power bank correctly in your carry-on at home. Then you reach the gate, the overhead bins are full and the agent tags your carry-on to go underneath the plane.

At that moment, your carry-on has become checked luggage.

Before handing it over, remove:.

The easiest system is to keep all power banks and spare batteries in one small pouch inside your personal item. If your roller bag gets gate-checked, you can remove the pouch in seconds instead of digging through your suitcase while the boarding line gives you the collective death stare.

Airlines measure lithium-ion battery size in watt-hours, written as Wh.

Most standard phone power banks are under 100 Wh and are usually allowed in carry-on baggage. Larger batteries may require airline approval, and very large batteries are generally not allowed in normal passenger baggage.

The 100 Wh rule matters most for large laptop power banks, professional camera gear, video equipment and drone batteries.

A typical 10,000 mAh power bank is often around 37 Wh. A 20,000 mAh power bank is often around 74 Wh. Larger power banks can get close to the limit, so check before you pack.

According to CATSA’s battery packing guidelines, travellers should keep batteries and electronic devices containing batteries in their carry-on baggage, avoid damaged or recalled batteries, and protect spare batteries from short-circuiting.

Recent findings suggest that look for the Wh rating printed on the back, bottom or side of the power bank. Newer batteries often show this number clearly.

If the label only demonstrates mAh and volts, you can calculate watt-hours with this formula:.

Since 1,000 mAh equals 1 Ah, a 20,000 mAh power bank is 20 Ah.

That would usually fall under the 100 Wh carry-on limit.

It has been revealed that if the label has rubbed off and the airline cannot confirm the battery rating, the item may be refused. Do not rely on guessing at the airport.

Laptops, phones and tablets have batteries installed inside the device, so they are not treated the same way as loose spare batteries or power banks.

However, airline rules vary. If an airline allows these devices in checked luggage, they should be completely powered off, protected from damage and packed so they cannot accidentally turn on.

That means fully powered off, not sleeping, hibernating or sitting there quietly planning to wake up mid-flight.

Sources indicate that in practice, keep phones, laptops and tablets in the cabin whenever possible. They are valuable, easy to damage and often essential if your checked bag is delayed.

Recent findings suggest that no. Vapes and e-cigarettes should not be packed in checked luggage because they contain batteries. They should travel in the cabin and must not be used or charged during the flight.

According to recent reports, rules for vaping products also vary by destination, and some countries restrict or ban them. If an adult is legally travelling with one, it still needs to follow airline battery rules.

Sources indicate that if you are packing for someone else, check for these before closing a checked suitcase. A vape tossed into checked luggage can create the same battery issue as other lithium-powered devices.

Smart luggage can usually be checked only if the battery can be removed.

A smart bag is luggage with built-in charging, tracking or other battery-powered features. If the bag is going into the cabin and meets carry-on size limits, it may be accepted as a carry-on. If it has to be checked, the battery must usually be removed and brought into the cabin.

If the battery cannot be removed, the airline may refuse to accept the bag as checked luggage.

Before travelling with smart luggage, find the battery compartment at home. Do not wait until the check-in counter to discover that the “removable” battery requires a tiny screwdriver, a prayer and the patience of a saint.

The drone or camera body may be allowed in checked luggage by some airlines, but spare lithium batteries should be removed and carried in the cabin.

Spare camera batteries and drone batteries should be individually protected so the terminals cannot touch metal or each other. Use the original packaging, a battery case, a protective pouch or tape over exposed terminals.

In a recent development, if you travel with several batteries for photography or video work, check your airline’s quantity limits before you fly. Battery rules can be stricter for professional video gear and larger drone batteries.

Loose batteries should never be thrown into a bag with coins, keys, jewellery, cables or other metal objects. Battery terminals can short-circuit if they touch metal.

This is especially important for camera batteries, drone batteries and loose rechargeable cells.

Do not travel with a battery that is swollen, cracked, leaking, unusually hot, damaged or recalled.

A swollen power bank is not “probably fine.” It is a damaged battery and should be taken to an appropriate recycling or disposal location.

Before flying with an older power bank, check the model number and look for current recall notices from the manufacturer or your government recall site. Some recalled power banks may be prohibited onboard entirely.

If a battery looks questionable, leave it at home. Replacing a charger is cheaper than dealing with a safety incident at the airport.

If a battery or device becomes hot, starts swelling, smokes, sparks or smells strange during a flight, tell the cabin crew immediately.

Do not put it in the overhead bin. Do not hide it in a bag. Do not take it to the washroom. Cabin crew are trained to respond to battery incidents, but they need to know right away.

Industry observers note that the goal is not to handle the problem yourself. The goal is to alert the people trained to deal with it.

Before leaving for the airport, do this quick check:.

This takes less than two minutes and can prevent a pulled bag, confiscated item or airport delay.

Before you check a suitcase or hand over a carry-on at the gate, make sure:.

Before you check any bag, open it and look for batteries.

It has been revealed that power banks, portable chargers, spare batteries and removable lithium batteries stay with you in the cabin. Phones, laptops, tablets and cameras are usually safer in your carry-on. If your carry-on gets taken at the gate, remove your battery pouch before the bag goes underneath the plane.

The goal is not to stop travelling with electronics. The goal is to stop packing them on autopilot.

A two-minute battery check before every flight can save your bag, your gear and possibly your travel day.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“The bottom line is we need to understand the magnitude of this with respect to Chinese intelligence, possible chip diversion,” noted Rep. John Moolenaar, R-Mich., seen above. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call file photo).

The resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on Thursday did little to quell bipartisan demands from Congress for an accounting of potential national security fallout from his affair with an alleged Chinese spy and talk of adding tougher chip export controls to the annual defense authorization bill.

Industry observers note that huang admitted on Sunday to having an affair, and reports say that it was with Alice Huang, an executive at Singaporean tech tech giant and Nvidia customer Megaspeed, whom the U.S. government believes spied for China, according to recent reports. The New York Times and Reuters reported he also had affairs with two Nvidia employees.

Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., told reporters Thursday that he supports the Senate investigating Huang’s potential influence on U.S. artificial intelligence and chip policy.

“I think that it would make sense because of the… nature of the association… and the governments and the national security interests we were talking about here,” Thune remarked, though he said he thought it would be “wrong” to make assumptions about how close Huang’s relationship with President Donald Trump has been.

Industry observers note that senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y., echoed the need for lawmakers to delve into the scandal, saying in a post on X that “Congress must demand answers.”.

Recent findings suggest that “The Trump administration must also answer for what it did once it learned about Mr. Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset. Were government officials told not to investigate because of Trump’s relationship with Mr. Huang? What did Trump know when he personally invited Mr. Huang aboard Air Force One?” Schumer wrote, referring to the president having invited Huang to accompany him to China in May.

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., noted at a press conference that Reps. Gregory W. Meeks, D-N.Y., and Jim Himes, D-Conn., the ranking members of the Foreign Affairs and Intelligence committees, respectively, are leading Democrats’ efforts to “get to the bottom of what has happened.”.

“We need a classified briefing made available to members of Congress as it relates to the Nvidia situation,” Jeffries stated. “And to the extent that our national security has been compromised, the American people deserve answers, and we're going to work to make sure that happens.”.

The investigations look likely to begin before control of Congress changes hands in January.

It has been revealed that rep. John Moolenaar, R-Mich., who chairs the House select China committee, told reporters that his panel, along with House Foreign Affairs and Intelligence, are in negotiations with Huang to find a date for his testimony before Congress.

“The bottom line is we need to understand the magnitude of this with respect to Chinese intelligence, possible chip diversion,” Moolenaar said. “What ways is Chinese intelligence influencing his perspective, his perspective influencing national security policy?”.

Recent findings suggest that last week, the chairs of the three committees sent a letter to Huang requesting that he appear at a joint closed-door briefing. Moolenaar said that if Huang does not agree to a date, the committees will subpoena him.

Recent findings suggest that late Thursday, he joined with House Foreign Affairs Chairman Brian Mast, R-Fla., and House Intelligence Chairman Rick Crawford, R-Ark., in sending a new letter to Huang seeking a closed-door transcribed interview on Dec. 1. They also wrote to Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter seeking a similar interview on Dec. 2. Separately, Mast wrote to Jeffrey Kessler, the Commerce Department undersecretary for industry and security, seeking his appearance at a committee hearing on Dec. 3.

Moolenaar also said that Congress needs to understand what privileged information Chinese intelligence may have gained access to through Huang and how they may have tried to influence U.S. policy.

“We need to have strong safeguards when it comes to our technology and export controls,” Moolenaar said. “And [Huang has] been one of the strongest proponents for not having export controls. This shines a whole new light on that discussion.”.

Recent findings suggest that also late Thursday, Senate Banking Chairman Tim Scott, R-S.C.,  sent a letter to Huang calling on him to appear at a Dec. 3 committee hearing and another letter to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify at a Dec. 10 hearing "regarding recent public reports about NVIDIA and the Department of Commerce's role that raises national security concerns.".

Recent findings suggest that A proposed manager’s amendment to the Senate's fiscal 2027 National Defense Authorization Act bill (S 4784) contains several possibilities for those safeguards, including requirements for chip security mechanisms that would allow for verification if semiconductors are diverted to countries of concern and a ban on exporting certain very powerful chips to those countries. The House NDAA does not contain similar language.

Industry observers note that however, House Armed Services Chair Mike D. Rogers, D-Ala., is open to the restrictions. He told reporters Wednesday that he “would like to see” semiconductor export controls in the NDAA, but that the Huang scandal had not changed his position.

Democratic Caucus Vice Chair Ted Lieu, D-Calif., told reporters on Thursday that after reports that the federal government had been aware of Huang’s affair with the alleged spy, the administration should have shared the information with Congress.

“The administration needs to be investigated for hiding this information from Congress and the American people,” he remarked.

Lieu also suggested that Nvidia’s reported donation to the White House ballroom project influenced the Trump administration’s decision to allow the export of some powerful Nvidia chips to China.

It has been revealed that “There is no reason to do that. That hurts our national security, and we have an opportunity right now to fix that in the upcoming National Defense Authorization,” Lieu said.

Mast noted the Huang revelations could give latest momentum to including chip export rules in the NDAA. He also said that his “directive” on the issue came “straight from the admin” and informed his objectives on the committee.

Industry observers note that “Don't let chips be smuggled to China. Make sure that American companies get to buy them first,” Mast remarked. “Make sure that the machines that make them don't get sold to them, even though it's the Dutch that make the machines. Make sure that they can't access it remotely.”.

Mast’s committee has advanced many of those priorities, including some of the language included in the NDAA.

In March, the committee on a unanimous vote advanced legislation known as the Chip Security Act, which would require chip security mechanisms to verify that certain semiconductors subject to export controls aren’t diverted to countries of concern, including China and Iran.

The committee also advanced bills to require the Bureau of Industry and Security and the State Department to work with allied suppliers of semiconductor manufacturing equipment to implement export controls to prevent the equipment from going to countries of concern, and to require licenses for the export of certain powerful chips, including banning exporting certain chips to countries of concern.

Versions of all three bills are included in the Senate manager’s amendment to the NDAA.

The scandal has also led to calls for oversight of the Commerce Department, including Secretary Howard Lutnick, for its handling of export policy and actions around Huang.

Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., told reporters Thursday that Lutnick and Nvidia should testify “before Democrats can set the narrative.”.

“If there is some reasonable basis or some way to discount some of the reporting, the best way to do it is request a meeting with us and give us a briefing,” Tillis noted. “Because otherwise, you're going to get what you get in an oversight hearing in about six weeks.”.

It has been revealed that asked about oversight of the Commerce Department’s role in the Huang scandal, Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, who chairs the Commerce Committee, said his panel “has engaged in vigorous oversight under Republican presidents and Democrat presidents and will continue to be [engaged in it].”.

On Wednesday, prior to Huang’s resignation, Senate Banking ranking member Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., and Sen. Chris Coons, D-Del., sent a letter to Lutnick, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller requesting that they “preserve all documents, communications, records, and other materials regarding the export of NVIDIA’s advanced AI chips to China or to entities that may divert such chips to China.”.

“This incident raises significant concerns about the federal government’s ability to effectively enforce our export controls and protect our national security,” the senators wrote.

In a statement Thursday, Warren said that Huang’s resignation did not “absolve” him of the need to answer questions. She also called for the passage of stricter export controls, including the bill to ban the export of certain chips to China.

It has been revealed that sen. Michael Bennet, D-Colo., sent his own letter on Wednesday to Lutnick, Rubio, Attorney General Todd Blanche and Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, requesting an enhancement on the Justice Department’s investigation into Megaspeed for possibly diverting U.S. chips to China.

Savannah Behrmann, John M. Donnelly, Jacob Fulton and David Jordan contributed to this report.

  • Judge Frederico dos Santos Messias of the São Paulo State Court of Justice’s specialized maritime court granted the request from R11 Travel Viagens e Turismo against GLCL Global Cruiseline Ltd., the Cyprus-registered company that operates as Corazul.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that A Brazilian court ordered the arrest of Corazul’s the Buenavista at the Port of Santos after the cruise line’s exclusive Brazilian distributor claimed it was owed about $270,000 (R$1.48 million), according to a court decision dated Nov. 13.

Judge Frederico dos Santos Messias of the São Paulo State Court of Justice’s specialized maritime court granted the request from R11 Travel Viagens e Turismo against GLCL Global Cruiseline Ltd., the Cyprus-registered company that operates as Corazul.

The judge issued the order without first hearing from Corazul, the decision showed.

The order barred the Buenavista from leaving Brazilian waters. The court noted the ship was anchored off Santos for repairs.

The judge set security at about $323,000 (R$1.78 million) and mentioned the ship would be released if Corazul deposited that amount or posted a bank guarantee.

According to the decision, R11 said Corazul owed about $1.27 million (R$6.96 million) under a four-year exclusive distribution agreement signed in March. That figure included about $780,000 (EUR 675,000) in unpaid quarterly marketing contributions. After subtracting about $1 million (R$5.48 million) in passenger funds it held, R11 put the net balance at about $270,000.

Recent findings suggest that the filing, as summarized by the court, described a series of disruptions including the cancellation of the Buenavista’s European season in June; the cancellation of its Oct. 23 inaugural Brazilian cruise nine days before departure and complaints about onboard service on the Oct. 30 sailing. The company has since suspended operations and R11 has stopped selling cruises on the ship.

Recent findings suggest that R11 mentioned Corazul demanded $400,000 on Nov. 4 before it would operate the Nov. 6 departure. R11 refused.

The court noted that only two of the 11 sailings scheduled between Oct. 23 and Nov. 27 operated. Corazul also suspended operations until Nov. 30 and moved the end of its Brazil season up to March 5, 2027. The judge wrote that Corazul’s own communications showed a “serious liquidity collapse.”.

According to recent reports, the dispute is headed to arbitration in São Paulo under AMCHAM, the American Chamber of Commerce for Brazil. The decision stated that R11 must file within 30 days or the order lapses. Corazul has five days after being served to contest it.

Legislative Branch bill would hold off on GAO cuts

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, A group of visitors walks past the Capitol on Sept.
  • With stopgap funding set to expire in less than a month, Senate Republican appropriators Thursday unveiled a roughly $5.3 billion draft fiscal 2027 Legislative Branch spending bill that would boost security funding and sidestep contentious debates over a key watchdog.
  • The proposal would provide $965 million for Capitol Police, a nearly $83 million hike from fiscal 2026, but still short of the more than $1 billion the department requested as threats against lawmakers rise.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A group of visitors walks past the Capitol on Sept. 22. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call file photo).

With stopgap funding set to expire in less than a month, Senate Republican appropriators Thursday unveiled a roughly $5.3 billion draft fiscal 2027 Legislative Branch spending bill that would boost security funding and sidestep contentious debates over a key watchdog.

The proposal would provide $965 million for Capitol Police, a nearly $83 million hike from fiscal 2026, but still short of the more than $1 billion the department requested as threats against lawmakers rise.

And it would bump funding for the Government Accountability Office up to $860 million, an increase of nearly 6 percent from fiscal 2026. That stands in contrast to the version of the bill advanced by the House Appropriations Committee in May, which floated slashing the GAO by 25 percent.

It joins several other draft spending bills released this week by Senate Appropriations Chair Susan Collins, R-Maine, who is trying to kickstart bicameral negotiations as lawmakers stare down a Dec. 11 deadline to fund the government.

According to recent reports, her committee ran into a stalemate on topline numbers earlier this year that stopped it from marking up any of the 12 annual bills, but lawmakers nipped the threat of a government shutdown in the bud ahead of the midterm elections by pushing through a continuing resolution. With that funding now set to expire next month, appropriators are hoping they can wrap up at least some of the bills while punting the rest into the next Congress with another stopgap.

The Legislative Branch bill is the smallest of the 12 appropriations bills and typically among the least controversial. But debates over the GAO have become a sticking point during the Trump administration as the agency accuses the White House of violating budget laws — a move the Office of Management and Budget has pushed back on, arguing the GAO has no authority over the administration since it is part of the legislative branch.

In a recent development, the GAO has been without a permanent head after its longtime leader Gene L. Dodaro retired last year, although Republicans are now making a last-ditch effort to get one confirmed during the lame-duck session before Democrats take power.

The House version of the spending bill sought to bar the comptroller general from suing under the 1974 budget law restricting presidential impoundments, unless specifically authorized by Congress. But the Senate proposal includes no such language, and overall, it appears designed to avoid drastic or contentious moves.

It would also leave in place a provision that would block cost-of-living adjustments for members of Congress, whose pay has been frozen since 2009.

Senate Democrats, however, criticized the bill text after its release, saying it wouldn’t invest enough in the legislative branch.

“The Legislative Branch bill underfunds key work to support oversight of the Executive Branch, and it underfunds key efforts to keep the Capitol complex safe,” Senate Appropriations ranking member Patty Murray, D-Wash., mentioned in a statement.

Sources indicate that the Architect of the Capitol would get $762.5 million, though funding for House office buildings is not included in that total. The agency is requesting $1.6 billion as it seeks to begin large-scale renovations of the Rayburn House Office Building. The architect has repeatedly warned lawmakers that parts of the Capitol complex are in need of critical infrastructure upgrades, arguing that delaying renovations will only make them more expensive as things continue to deteriorate.

The bill’s $5.3 billion proposal represents funding for the Senate and legislative branch agencies, while excluding House-only funds, which are typically added later.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the buzz of the Venice Film Festival has only just died down, when I step out of a Riva boat that bobs at the berth of the Hotel Cipriani Venice on Giudecca Island. I’m excited but also exhausted after spending the previous ten days on several long-haul flights, and I fear it’s beginning to affect my conversational skills—and my collagen levels. Luckily, I’m not here to attend a premiere or hop between Biennale events. I'm here to experience Cipriani's newly opened Dior Spa, the fashion house's first in Venice.

Venice’s links with Dior go back to 1951 when the French couture brand’s eponymous founder fell in love with the city after attending the Ball of the Century costume party at the Palazzo Labia, hosted by art collector Charles de Beistegui.

The views from my suite's private terrace.

A welcome Dior takeover on Cip's ground floor.

It has been revealed that sophia Loren and Julia Roberts are just a few of the starry names to have stayed at this classic hotel, which launched its upcoming spa in July 2026 as part of ongoing renovations led by New York architect Peter Marino. The cream and pastel palette channels an 18th-century Venetian Rococo spirit, with elegant mid-century Italian stucco and terrazzo flooring. Science-driven skincare nerds tend to believe that fashion houses can’t run beauty departments worthy of their approval, but Dior has the potential to persuade them otherwise. Many luxury spas are often either visually stunning temples that offer underwhelming treatments, or medically-driven centers that leave you glowing but feeling as if you’re in a hospital. Dior combines the best of both worlds, recalling an old-school glamour while deploying higher-tech treatments that aren’t geared towards “maxxing” but aim for clients to look and feel their best in a tranquil environment.

The Dior Spa's La Collection Privée island.

One of the Dior Spa's Murano chandeliers.

Recent findings suggest that after spending the morning in Murano watching the world’s most talented glassblowers at work, I head down to the spa’s marbled entrance where a Murano chandelier dangles above a centerpiece table festooned with beautiful bottles of parfums from Dior’s La Collection Privée, including Tobacolore and, my favorite fragrance, La Colle Noire. I’m handed a rose infusion before slipping into cloud-soft Dior slippers and waiting outside my treatment room for one of the signature treatments, which include Le Théâtre Corporal, a four-handed, Ayurvedic-inspired massage (which couples can do together), and the Golden Aura hydrafacial. But I’m here for what feels like the most apt option in a city famed for its masked balls: the Mascarade facial.

Setting up for a canalside Dior masterclass.

Developed by the brand’s global skincare ambassador, Hadda Akrim, the Mascarade aims to regenerate the skin and soothe the mind. I’m in need of it now that my circadian rhythm is disrupted after back-to-back flights, cabin pressure and changing time zones. The treatment is more than just a facial: it involves 90 minutes of drainage, rebalancing, and re-boosting with the help of devices that encourage the nutrients being massaged into your skin to sink deeper. Firstly, I lie on the treatment table to receive an abdominal massage, which rebalances my nervous system (the gut is our second brain, after all) and restores my inner harmony to maximize my radiance.

Next, ultrasound waves are applied across my face to improve the skin’s elasticity and circulation, followed by microcurrent muscle stimulation during which I literally feel my cells awakening. The procedure soothes my mind so much I fall into a contented sleep. It’s all designed to boost my complexion’s glow—and it works. Dior’s global spa director, Olivier Hahn, told me he’s most proud of the sonic component of the spa offering, which does its job by calming me down without me even noticing.

A heavenly breakfast in my top-floor suite.

The best kind of antioxidants at Oro restaurant.

Sources indicate that I wake up for the next stage of the treatment, a technical jaw massage, which the facialist carries out to counteract my nighttime teeth-grinding. She then places cryogenic stones over a cooling mask to firm, drain, and reoxygenate my skin. It’s a perfect way to re-enter the world, cognitively and physically. I feel snatched as I sip coffee by the pool after the treatment. The Mascarade facial is great for a morning-after depuffing, but, given the OMGs I receive from fellow spa-goers, I conclude that it’s also perfect for an evening out. I head out into the Venetian night with nothing but a touch of mascara and a post-facial luminosity.

Feeling like a kid on Christmas morning, the staff sent me on my way with a bag of the Dior Prestige products to keep up my skincare routine back home. The ingredients are mainly organic, something I hadn’t expected. In the same way that historic French vineyards downplay their organic practices for fear of alienating clients disdainful of natural wines, Dior also keeps its products' natural roots on the down low. It all comes as a pleasant surprise and further cements this spa’s authority in the world of regenerative beauty therapy.

  • The first is a “Cruise Plus” brand renewal strategy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the 2026 Wusongkou Forum took place on Nov. 8 at the Shanghai International Cruise Tourism Resort in Baoshan. It brought together regulators, port authorities, cruise operators and industry experts to discuss what organizers called “three-cruise synergy,” which is the coordinated development of ocean cruise ships, river cruise vessels and yachts.

According to recent reports, hosted by Shanghai Wusongkou Culture & Tourism Investment (Group) Co., the event included the launch of a “Three-Cruise Synergy · A Fresh Voyage from River to Sea” program. Four initiatives were announced.

The first is a “Cruise Plus” brand renewal strategy. It targets four consumer segments: seniors, weddings and romance travel, sporting events and younger travelers. The goal is to turn passenger volume into more onboard and shoreside spending.

The second is a river-sea linkage project that uses Wusongkou’s location at the mouth of the Yangtze to connect inland river cities with ocean itineraries. Its flagship product is the Yangtze No. 3, which has begun sailing between Chongqing and Shanghai from the Wusongkou International Cruise Terminal. It is the first river-sea cruise service to cover the full length of the Yangtze.

Third, China Huaxia International Cruise Co. released October 2026 data for its China Cruise Consumption Vitality Index. The company described it as the country’s first regular data tool for the cruise market.

The fourth initiative links the cruise terminal with Shanghai Baoshan railway station, which is due to open next year as the meeting point of the Shanghai–Chongqing–Chengdu high-speed line and the Shanghai–Nantong railway. Aims include combined rail and cruise ticketing, a direct shuttle, baggage transfer from car door to cabin door and shared VIP benefits.

On forum day, the Adora Magic City and the Adora Flora City, China’s first two domestically built large cruise ships, were berthed together at Wusongkou for the first time.
